title: Localization and Internationalization
keywords: accessibility, performance, debugging, and professional practice
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of localization and internationalization and when it is appropriate.
Apply language attributes using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check long text and translated interfaces and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study localization and internationalization and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Localization and Internationalization makes the interface more robust for real users and real content. Measure and reproduce behavior, inspect semantics and focus, and document the browser, viewport, steps, and result so another developer can repeat the check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating localization and internationalization as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
